blocks.text: קְרִיאַת הַתּוֹרָה לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
uncertainties: Running header; the page number 73 is printed on both sides. The pointing is small and was read at low resolution.

blocks.text: Before reading from the Torah, the individual called upon says the following:
בָּרְכוּ אֶת־יְיָ הַמְבֹרָךְ:
Cong.
בָּרוּךְ יְיָ הַמְבֹרָךְ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
He then repeats this and continues:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ, אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר בָּֽחַר־בָּֽנוּ מִכָּל־הָעַמִּים, וְנָֽתַן־לָֽנוּ אֶת־תּוֹרָתוֹ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ, נוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה:
uncertainties: There are small vertical strokes under בחר, בנו, ונתן and לנו. I recorded them as meteg, but they are not certain.
The word מִכָּל was read as dagesh plus qamats qatan. The scan cannot show the difference between qamats types.

blocks.text: Then the reading of the Torah begins until the end of the portion when the individual who had been called upon, says:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ, אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר נָֽתַן־לָֽנוּ תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת, וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם נָטַע בְּתוֹכֵֽנוּ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ, נוֹתֵן הַתּוֹרָה:
uncertainties: The meteg on נָֽתַן, לָֽנוּ and בְּתוֹכֵֽנוּ is uncertain.
There is a small mark near the shin of אֲשֶׁר that may be a meteg or a print artifact.

blocks.text: וקורין בס״ת ראשון וה׳ פקד את שרה בפרשת וירא.
uncertainties: This line is set in small Rashi-style type. I read the first word as וקורין; the final letters are unclear and could be וקורים.
I could not confirm the exact abbreviation mark in בס״ת.

blocks.text: וַיהוָה פָּקַד אֶת־שָׂרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמָר וַיַּעַשׂ יְהוָה לְשָׂרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּר:
uncertainties: Cantillation is printed but not transcribed; see notes.
In אָמָר, the second vowel is pausal qamats with an accent.

blocks.text: Torah Reading for the New Year
Before reading from the Torah, the individual called upon says the following:
ברכו
Bless the Lord who is called blessed.
The congregation responds:
ברוך
Blessed is the Lord who is called blessed, for ever and ever.
He then repeats this and continues:
ברוך
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has chosen us from all peoples and given us His Torah. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, giver of the Torah.
Then the reading of the Torah begins until the end of the portion when the individual who had been called upon, says:
ברוך
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has given us the Torah of truth and implanted in us eternal life. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, giver of the Torah.
Reading from the First Torah Scroll
(Genesis: Chapter 21)

blocks.reference: Genesis 21:1–9 (beginning; continues on next English page)
blocks.text: The Lord considered Sarah just as He had said and the Lord did for Sarah just as He had spoken. And Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age at the appointed time which God had told him. Abraham called the name of his son, who was born to him, whom Sarah had born to him, Isaac. Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old just as God had commanded him. Abraham was a hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born to him. Then Sarah said: ‘God has given me mirth; everyone who hears of it will laugh with me’. She said: ‘Who would have foretold to Abraham that Sarah would suckle children; yet have I born him a son in his old age’. The child grew and was weaned; and Abraham prepared a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned. Then Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian
uncertainties: This is one continuous paragraph with no verse numbers; it breaks off mid-sentence at the bottom of the page.
The English has no equivalent of the Hebrew aliyah labels (לוי and the Shabbat marker).
The printed spelling 'born' (for 'borne') and the placement of the closing quotation marks before the full stops are kept as printed.

notes: CONTRARY TO THE BRIEF: the Torah text on s168 (Genesis 21:1–9) clearly has full cantillation marks in the enlarged bands, including conjunctive and disjunctive accents on almost every word. I could not reliably identify every accent at this resolution, and supplying them from memory was forbidden. So the verse blocks give consonants, vowels and maqaf only, and leave out the accents. These verses need a separate pass for cantillation.

Because of that, I cannot fully certify the vowels in the verse blocks. The consonants were checked against the bands. Some vowel details (qubbuts, rafe versus dagesh, the dagesh in לּוֹ) were hard to see and could be confused with nearby accent marks.
In Genesis 21:7, after מִלֵּל, there is a raised vertical/oblique mark before לְאַבְרָהָם. It is probably pasek, or the vertical stroke of a legarmeh. It is flagged, not transcribed.
No marginal qere/ketiv notes were found on either page.
Inline aliyah labels on s168: 'לוי' between verses 4 and 5, and the parenthetical before verse 9, tentatively read as '(בשבת ג.)'. The parenthetical reading is uncertain.
Page breaks: Genesis 21:9 continues past the bottom of both pages. The Hebrew stops at 'אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָה' and the English at 'the son of Hagar the Egyptian'.
The Hebrew words ברכו and ברוך in the English column are cue words linking to the Hebrew. They are not translated prayer text.
